entity.name: Francis of Assisi
entity.description: The rich kid who stripped naked in court to renounce his inheritance and embrace poverty. Founded the Franciscan Order, walked unarmed into a Crusader battlefield to meet the Sultan of Egypt, and reportedly received the stigmata. Patron saint of animals and Italy, and namesake of San Francisco.

story.name: Francis of Assisi
story.description: A silk merchant's son strips naked to renounce wealth, founds a mendicant order, crosses Crusade lines to meet the Sultan, and receives mysterious wounds matching Christ's. The life of medieval Christianity's most radical reformer.

moments.name: Francis of Assisi Strips Naked to Renounce His Wealthy Father
moments.subtitle: A silk merchant's son trades his inheritance for a beggar's life
moments.description: In 1206, before the Bishop of Assisi, a young man named Francis publicly renounced his father Pietro di Bernardone, a wealthy silk merchant, and all claims to his family's fortune. According to multiple accounts, Francis stripped off his fine clothes in the public square as a symbol of total renunciation, and the bishop covered him with his own cloak. Francis had been selling his father's cloth to fund church repairs after a mystical vision at San Damiano chapel. The dramatic break launched Francis into a life of voluntary poverty that would reshape Western Christianity.

moments.name: Pope Innocent III Approves the Franciscan Order in Rome
moments.subtitle: A barefoot preacher convinces the most powerful man in Christendom
moments.description: On 16 April 1210, Pope Innocent III formally endorsed a new religious order founded by Francis of Assisi after reportedly dreaming that Francis was holding up the collapsing Lateran Basilica. Francis had arrived in Rome with 11 followers and a simple rule drawn from Bible verses. The Pope's counselors considered the proposed life of absolute poverty impractical and dangerous, but Innocent overruled them. The Order of Friars Minor, known as the Franciscans, grew from those 12 men into one of the largest religious orders in history, with tens of thousands of members within Francis's lifetime.

moments.name: Francis of Assisi Crosses Crusade Lines to Meet the Sultan of Egypt
moments.subtitle: An unarmed friar walks into an enemy camp during a holy war
moments.description: During the Fifth Crusade in 1219, Francis of Assisi traveled to Egypt where Crusader forces had been besieging the city of Damietta for over a year. Accompanied only by Friar Illuminatus, Francis crossed the battle lines and entered the camp of Sultan al-Kamil, hoping to convert him to Christianity or achieve martyrdom. The Sultan received Francis with courtesy and listened to his preaching, though no conversion took place. The encounter became one of the most celebrated episodes of interfaith dialogue in medieval history, and remains a touchstone for Christian-Muslim relations eight centuries later.

moments.name: Francis of Assisi Reportedly Receives the Stigmata on Mount La Verna
moments.subtitle: The first recorded case of a person bearing wounds matching Christ's crucifixion
moments.description: In September 1224, while fasting and praying on the remote mountain of La Verna in Tuscany, Francis of Assisi reportedly experienced a vision of a seraphic angel and afterward displayed wounds on his hands, feet, and side resembling those of the crucified Christ. This was the first recorded case of stigmata in Christian history. The event was witnessed by several companions and documented within years of its occurrence. Whether miraculous or medical, the stigmata cemented Francis's status as the most Christ-like figure in medieval Christianity. He was canonized just two years after his death.
moments.address: Sanctuary of La Verna, Chiusi della Verna, Tuscany, Italy

moments.name: Francis of Assisi Dies at Age 44 at the Porziuncola Chapel
moments.subtitle: The founder of a global religious order dies owning nothing
moments.description: On 3 October 1226, Francis of Assisi died at the Porziuncola, the tiny chapel of St. Mary of the Angels near Assisi that had served as the cradle of his religious movement. Francis was 44 years old and had spent the final two years of his life in declining health, nearly blind and bearing the stigmata wounds. He asked to be laid naked on the bare ground to die as he had lived, in complete poverty. Pope Gregory IX canonized Francis less than two years later on 16 July 1228, making him one of the fastest canonizations in Church history.
moments.address: Basilica of Santa Maria degli Angeli, Assisi, Italy
